context.analysis:
## Overview
[The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a modern Azure platform while the legacy system remains the system of record. It enables online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining strict data consistency and a 3-year hybrid migration timeline.]

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers
- New Claims Platform (Azure App Service, Azure SQL)
- Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2, On-Premise)
- Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD (Identity Provider)
- Analytics & Reporting System (Azure Synapse / Power BI)
- Azure API Management (APM) Gateway

## Relationships
- Customers & Brokers -> New Claims Platform via HTTPS for online claim submission
- Claims Adjusters -> New Claims Platform via HTTPS for web application access
- New Claims Platform <-> Legacy Mainframe via Azure ExpressRoute, mTLS, and Azure API Management
- New Claims Platform -> Analytics & Reporting System via Azure Event Hubs using TLS 1.3
- Users -> Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD via OAuth 2.0 / OIDC for Single Sign-On

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service and Azure SQL for hosting the modern platform due to managed cloud capabilities
- Azure API Management (APM) for rate-limiting, token validation, and protecting fragile mainframe interfaces
- Azure ExpressRoute and mTLS for secure, encrypted hybrid connectivity between Azure and on-premise infrastructure
- Azure Application Insights for distributed tracing across hybrid latency boundaries
- OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (OIDC) via Azure AD / Entra ID for secure single sign-on

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates the legacy mainframe from excessive direct queries using an Azure API Management gateway and asynchronous event streams, ensuring business continuity and compliance with strict batch window constraints. Furthermore, leveraging managed Azure services mitigates the team's low cloud experience while supporting rapid, incremental claim type migrations with automated rollback capabilities.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old legacy mainframe claims system by gradually migrating claim types to a hybrid Azure cloud platform. It ensures continuous processing, strict data consistency, and rapid one-day fallback capabilities without disrupting nightly batch windows.

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers
- Legacy Mainframe
- Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD
- Analytics & Reporting System
- Customer/Broker Portal
- Adjuster Workstation
- Integration & Routing Engine
- Observability & Audit Logging
- Azure API Management Gateway

## Relationships
- End Customers and Brokers -> Customer/Broker Portal (HTTPS)
- Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers -> Adjuster Workstation (HTTPS)
- Customer/Broker Portal & Adjuster Workstation -> Integration & Routing Engine (HTTPS / AMQP)
- Integration & Routing Engine -> Azure API Management Gateway (HTTPS)
- Azure API Management Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe (Azure ExpressRoute, mTLS)
- Integration & Routing Engine -> Analytics & Reporting System (Azure Event Hubs, TLS 1.3)
- End Customers and Brokers & Claims Adjusters -> Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC)
- All Containers -> Observability & Audit Logging (HTTPS)

## Technology Stack
- Customer/Broker Portal: Azure App Service, React (Public SPA and BFF)
- Adjuster Workstation: Azure App Service, Angular (Internal UI optimized for sub-2s loads)
- Integration & Routing Engine: Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions (Asynchronous queuing, DLQ, and deduplication)
- Observability & Audit Logging: Azure Application Insights, Azure Cosmos DB (Distributed tracing and state tracking)
- Azure API Management Gateway: Azure API Management (Rate-limiting, token validation, and mainframe protection)
- Secret Management: Azure Key Vault (Managed identities and automated rotation)

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates user interfaces and encapsulates migration routing logic within the integration layer to meet strict performance targets and guarantee a one-day mainframe fallback. Asynchronous queuing and centralized observability protect fragile on-premise components while preventing lost or duplicated claims during the incremental transition.

Customer/Broker Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-based platform. It enables online claim submissions and adjuster workflows while maintaining legacy operations.

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers [person, context]
- Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers [person, context]
- Customer/Broker Portal [container, container] (Azure App Service, React)
- Adjuster Workstation [container, container] (Azure App Service, Angular)
- Integration & Routing Engine [container, container] (Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions)
- Azure API Management Gateway [container, container] (Azure API Management)
- Observability & Audit Logging [container, container] (Azure Application Insights, Azure Cosmos DB)
- Secret Management [container, container] (Azure Key Vault)
- Legacy Mainframe [externalSystem, context]
- Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD [externalSystem, context]

## Relationships
- Customer/Broker Portal -> Integration & Routing Engine [HTTPS / AMQP, TLS 1.3]
- Adjuster Workstation -> Integration & Routing Engine [HTTPS / AMQP, TLS 1.3]
- Integration & Routing Engine -> Azure API Management Gateway [HTTPS]
- Azure API Management Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe [Azure ExpressRoute, mTLS]
- End Customers and Brokers -> Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD [OAuth 2.0 / OIDC]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts public portals and internal workstations for managed hosting.
- React / Angular: Frontend frameworks for UI rendering and state management.
- ASP.NET Core: Powers BFF APIs for native Azure integration and security controls.
- Azure Service Bus: Handles asynchronous messaging, deduplication, and dead-letter queues.
- Azure API Management: Protects legacy mainframe endpoints with rate-limiting and token validation.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the fragile legacy mainframe behind secure Azure integration layers while enabling gradual, low-risk claim type migration. Standardizing on managed Azure services reduces operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience.

Integration & Routing Engine.analysis:
## Overview
- This system gradually modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe claims system by introducing a hybrid cloud platform while the legacy system processes active claims.
- The core purpose is to migrate claim types incrementally with zero data loss, low adjuster latency, and a reliable mainframe fallback mechanism.

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers [person]
- Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers [person]
- Legacy Mainframe [externalSystem]
- Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD [externalSystem]
- Analytics & Reporting System [externalSystem]
- Customer/Broker Portal [container] (Azure App Service, React)
- Adjuster Workstation [container] (Azure App Service, Angular)
- Integration & Routing Engine [container] (Azure Service Bus, Azure Functions)
- Claim Router Component [component] (.NET Isolated Azure Functions)
- Deduplication & State Component [component] (Azure Cosmos DB)
- Fallback Switch Component [component] (Azure App Configuration)
- Retry & DLQ Handler Component [component] (.NET Azure Functions)
- Azure API Management Gateway [container] (Azure API Management)
- Observability & Audit Logging [container] (Azure Application Insights, Azure Cosmos DB)
- Secret Management [container] (Azure Key Vault)

## Relationships
- End Customers and Brokers -> Customer/Broker Portal: Submit claims [HTTPS]
- Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers -> Adjuster Workstation: Manage claims [HTTPS]
- Customer/Broker Portal -> Integration & Routing Engine: Route claim submissions [HTTPS / AMQP]
- Adjuster Workstation -> Integration & Routing Engine: Route adjuster actions [HTTPS / AMQP]
- Integration & Routing Engine -> Azure API Management Gateway: Forward traffic [HTTPS]
- Azure API Management Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe: Access legacy records [Azure ExpressRoute, mTLS]
- Integration & Routing Engine -> Analytics & Reporting System: Stream event data [Azure Event Hubs, TLS 1.3]
- All Containers -> Observability & Audit Logging: Send telemetry [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service: Hosts user portals with managed infrastructure scaling.
- Azure Functions (Premium Plan): Provides serverless execution with pre-warmed instances to mitigate cold starts.
- Azure Service Bus: Manages asynchronous queuing, AMQP delivery, and Dead-Letter Queues.
- Azure Cosmos DB: Enforces idempotency and tracks state for deduplication.
- Azure App Configuration: Dynamically manages routing rules for the 1-day mainframe fallback.
- Azure API Management: Protects fragile mainframe interfaces with rate-limiting and validation.

## Rationale
- This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe dependencies while delivering a modern, responsive user experience.
- Managed Azure services reduce operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience while guaranteeing strict compliance with consistency and security requirements.

## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old regional insurer COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims platform through a hybrid cloud architecture. It provides online claim submission and adjuster workflows while ensuring continuous legacy synchronization and auditability.]

## Key Elements
* End Customers and Brokers
* Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers
* Legacy Mainframe
* Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD
* Analytics & Reporting System
* New Claims Platform
* Azure API Management (APM) Gateway
* Customer/Broker Portal
* Adjuster Workstation
* Integration & Routing Engine
* Observability & Audit Logging
* Secret Management

## Relationships
* End Customers and Brokers -> New Claims Platform [HTTPS]
* Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers -> New Claims Platform [HTTPS]
* New Claims Platform -> Legacy Mainframe [Azure ExpressRoute, mTLS, Azure API Management]
* New Claims Platform -> Analytics & Reporting System [Azure Event Hubs, TLS 1.3]
* Customer/Broker Portal -> Integration & Routing Engine [HTTPS / AMQP]
* Adjuster Workstation -> Integration & Routing Engine [HTTPS / AMQP]
* Integration & Routing Engine -> Azure API Management Gateway [HTTPS]
* Azure API Management Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe [Azure ExpressRoute, mTLS]

## Technology Stack
* Azure App Service: Hosts React portal and Angular workstation for low-latency UIs.
* Azure Functions & Azure Service Bus: Powers asynchronous queueing, routing, and audit event processing.
* Azure Cosmos DB Ledger mode: Ensures immutable, cryptographically verified audit trails for R-04 consistency.
* Azure Application Insights: Provides distributed telemetry and tracing across hybrid environments.
* Azure API Management: Protects legacy mainframe interfaces and handles rate-limiting.
* Azure Key Vault: Manages secrets, connection keys, and automated 90-day rotation.

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe interfaces while enabling incremental cloud migration of claim types. It guarantees transactional consistency and fast UI response times despite legacy latency constraints.]

## Overview
The system modernizes a regional insurer's 30-year-old mainframe claims system via a hybrid architecture. It securely routes claims, manages authentication, and gradually migrates claim types.

## Key Elements
- End Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers
- Legacy Mainframe
- Corporate Active Directory / Azure AD
- Analytics & Reporting System
- New Claims Platform
- Azure API Management Gateway
- Customer/Broker Portal
- Adjuster Workstation
- Integration & Routing Engine
- Observability & Audit Logging
- Secret Management (Azure Key Vault)

## Relationships
- End Customers and Brokers -> Customer/Broker Portal (HTTPS)
- Claims Adjusters and Claims Managers -> Adjuster Workstation (HTTPS)
- Customer/Broker Portal -> Integration & Routing Engine (HTTPS / AMQP)
- Adjuster Workstation -> Integration & Routing Engine (HTTPS / AMQP)
- Integration & Routing Engine -> Azure API Management Gateway (HTTPS)
- Azure API Management Gateway -> Legacy Mainframe (Azure ExpressRoute, mTLS)
- Integration & Routing Engine -> Analytics & Reporting System (Azure Event Hubs, TLS 1.3)
- Consuming containers -> Secret Management (HTTPS / Azure SDK)

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service & React/Angular: Hosts portal and workstation containers for fast, modern UI delivery.
- Azure Service Bus & Azure Functions: Powers asynchronous queuing and routing to protect fragile mainframe interfaces.
- Azure API Management: Provides rate-limiting, token validation, and mTLS protection for mainframe integration.
- Azure Key Vault & Managed Identities: Eliminates hardcoded credentials and secures sensitive keys and certificates.

## Rationale
The hybrid architecture protects fragile legacy systems while gradually migrating workloads to the cloud. Managed identities and robust API gateways ensure enterprise-grade security and maintainability without disrupting the strict batch window.
